Estimate a specific User Story, or feature, until a consensus is reached. This technique is particularly useful when refining the Product Backlog or conducting sprint planning and the team needs to focus on understanding a single User Story until an agreed upon estimate is reached.

To execute Planning Poker:

  1. Obtain the following:
    a. Planning Poker cards: these can be purchased or made by marking a set of cards with the Fibonacci sequence for each player (Note: EY branded planning poker cards exist)
    b. Set of selected Backlog Items requiring estimation

  2. Gather participants who will typically include the:
    a. Development Team – to discuss the Backlog Item and estimate it
    b. Product Owner (and relevant stakeholders) – to provide clarifications to the Development Team, as needed
    c. Scrum Master – to facilitate the process

  3. Distribute a set of cards to each Development Team member

  4. Establish a reference story and the estimate to deliver it if one has not already been agreed upon; or agree that estimates for delivered Backlog Items will serve as the reference point

  5. Next, the organizer initiates the session by reading aloud a Backlog Item

  6. The entire group discusses the Backlog Item, its nuances, expected outcomes and, only briefly, potential approach to complete it within a sprint; the Product Owner clarifies any queries about scope / acceptance criteria, this may result in the Backlog Item being modified

  7. Have participants select a number from their set of cards to indicate effort to deliver the Backlog Item; a 2 requiring twice as much effort to develop as an item classified as a 1 (and so on)

  8. All participants reveal the selected card at the same time
    a. If all participants have selected the same estimate it becomes the new estimate for the Backlog Item and the group moves on to the next Backlog Item
    b. If there is disagreement about the appropriate estimation, the participants who selected the highest and lowest duration should explain their rationale and the PO clarifies any areas of the Backlog Item that are not clear. Then everyone goes back to their cards and selects again until all participants agree on a particular estimate.
    c. In scenarios where a consensus is not being reached the team can agree to a tie-breaker approach, some options being:
    1. Designate the average of the highest rankings to be the estimate for that particular item
    2. Accept the highest ranking, or
    3. Dismiss an “outlier estimate” where only one team member has a different estimate than the rest of the team who is otherwise in agreement

Keep in mind with Planning Poker that:

  1. A reference point for relative Story Point measurement is always required
  2. Typical reference may vary depending on the size of the Product Backlog or the Sprint Backlog
  3. The common agreement may be to select which Backlog Item needs the minimum, maximum, or medium amount of effort.
  4. For minimum, maximum or medium effort the Backlog Item is assigned the corresponding Story Points and other Backlog Items are measured in relation to it.

The range of estimates used by any team or project for estimation of Backlog Items is typically limited to one of the following:

  1. Modified Fibonacci sequence – 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 20, 40, 100 / ∞ (Infinity) representing a story which cannot be estimated as it is too large. If you estimate the whole Product Backlog then you may agree larger maximum for Epics. However for sprint planning the maximum should be 100.
  2. Sequence of powers of 2 – 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128. If you estimate the whole Product Backlog then you may agree on larger maximum for Epics. However for sprint planning the maximum should be 128.

The reason for restricting the range of estimates is to both:

  1. Avoid misconceptions about accuracy of estimates (the bigger the item being estimated, the greater the uncertainty and therefore the larger the gaps between subsequent estimates to reflect this) and
  2. Limit lengthy debates within the team which do not add value such as being unable to choose between 13 and 14 Story Points which are in the error range for estimating
